q: Nuclear energy now provides about _____ of the world's electricity from about 450 nuclear power reactors.
e: Nuclear energy now provides about 10% of the world's electricity from about 450 nuclear power reactors. Put 20% or 50% in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. _____ of the world's electricity from about 450 nuclear power reactors. 10%.

q: A nuclear reaction is a process in which a particle or a gamma radiation penetrate into a nucleus and changes its _____.
e: A nuclear reaction is a process in which a particle or a gamma radiation penetrate into a nucleus and changes its configuration. charge is not configuration, and mass number only is not configuration either. Nuclear changes happen in the nucleus, not in the electron cloud of chemistry. Gamma decay dumps excitation energy as a photon; Z and A stay put.

q: From energy point of view, there are two types of nuclear reactions: exothermic reaction and _____ reaction.
e: From energy point of view, there are two types of nuclear reactions: exothermic reaction and endothermic reaction. Put isothermal or adiabatic in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A nuclear reaction is a particle or gamma entering a nucleus and rearranging it. Exothermic nuclear reactions lose mass; that mass defect leaves as energy.

q: If the total mass before a nuclear reaction takes place is greater than the total mass after reaction, this mass defect is released as energy and this type of reaction is known as _____ reaction.
e: If the total mass before a nuclear reaction takes place is greater than the total mass after reaction, this mass defect is released as energy and this type of reaction is known as exothermic reaction. Put endothermic or isothermal in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A nuclear reaction is a particle or gamma entering a nucleus and rearranging it. Exothermic nuclear reactions lose mass; that mass defect leaves as energy.

q: If the total mass before a nuclear reaction takes place is less than the total mass after reaction, external energy must be provided for the reaction to take place, known as _____ reaction.
e: If the total mass before a nuclear reaction takes place is less than the total mass after reaction, external energy must be provided for the reaction to take place, known as endothermic reaction. fission is not endothermic, and exothermic is not endothermic either. A nuclear reaction is a particle or gamma entering a nucleus and rearranging it. Endothermic nuclear reactions need extra energy because the products are heavier.

q: When a neutron strikes and penetrates a nucleus of uranium-235, the nucleus becomes highly unstable and splits into two lighter nuclei, shooting out two or three neutrons; this splitting process is called _____.
e: When a neutron strikes and penetrates a nucleus of uranium-235, the nucleus becomes highly unstable and splits into two lighter nuclei, shooting out two or three neutrons; this splitting process is called fission. Put fusion or decay in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A neutron is uncharged; fission starts when a neutron is absorbed by a heavy nucleus.

q: For a chain reaction to be maintained, the uranium-235 has to be above a certain _____ mass.
e: For a chain reaction to be maintained, the uranium-235 has to be above a certain critical mass. Put molar or atomic in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A chain reaction is when fission neutrons go on to split further fuel nuclei.

q: The energy released per atom in a nuclear reaction is about a _____ times greater than the energy released per atom from a chemical reaction.
e: The energy released per atom in a nuclear reaction is about a billion times greater than the energy released per atom from a chemical reaction. thousand is not billion, and million is not billion either. A nuclear reaction is a particle or gamma entering a nucleus and rearranging it.

q: Nuclear reactor is a device in which a fission chain reaction can be initiated, maintained and _____.
e: Nuclear reactor is a device in which a fission chain reaction can be initiated, maintained and controlled. Put accelerated or stopped completely in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A reactor is a vessel where a fission chain can be started, held, and steered.

q: Fissionable nuclear fuel is the material for fission reaction to take place, and _____ or plutonium-239 can be used as fuel.
e: Fissionable nuclear fuel is the material for fission reaction to take place, and uranium-235 or plutonium-239 can be used as fuel. Put carbon-14 or strontium-90 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Fission splits a heavy nucleus after a neutron bite, throwing fragments and more neutrons.

q: Neutrons released from a fission reaction are fast neutrons and they need to be slowed down to maintain a chain reaction by a material called _____.
e: Neutrons released from a fission reaction are fast neutrons and they need to be slowed down to maintain a chain reaction by a material called moderator. coolant and control rod belong to other processes, not this moderator case. Fission splits a heavy nucleus after a neutron bite, throwing fragments and more neutrons.

q: Graphite and ordinary water as well as heavy water are used as _____ in a nuclear reactor.
e: Graphite and ordinary water as well as heavy water are used as moderators in a nuclear reactor. coolants and shielding belong to other processes, not this moderators case. A reactor is a vessel where a fission chain can be started, held, and steered.

q: Water and carbon dioxide $CO_2$ gas are used as _____ in a nuclear reactor.
e: Water and carbon dioxide CO2 gas are used as coolant in a nuclear reactor. fuel is not coolant, and moderator is not coolant either. A reactor is a vessel where a fission chain can be started, held, and steered.

q: Control rods are used to control the rate of reaction by raising or lowering them from the core, and boron and _____ are used as control rods.
e: Control rods are used to control the rate of reaction by raising or lowering them from the core, and boron and cadmium are used as control rods. Put lead or uranium in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Control rods soak up neutrons; drop them in to quiet the pile, raise them to let it run.

q: Reactor vessel is to contain the reactor core, moderator, coolant and control rods, and it is a pressurized _____ vessel.
e: Reactor vessel is to contain the reactor core, moderator, coolant and control rods, and it is a pressurized steel vessel. Put concrete or glass in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Control rods soak up neutrons; drop them in to quiet the pile, raise them to let it run. Coolant carries fission-fragment heat out of the core before the metal melts.

q: Shielding is a protective barrier, usually a dense material, which reduces the passage of radiations from radioactive materials by _____ them.
e: Shielding is a protective barrier, usually a dense material, which reduces the passage of radiations from radioactive materials by absorbing them. Put reflecting or refracting in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Radioactivity is nuclear: an unstable nucleus emits alpha, beta, or gamma. Dense shielding soaks up radiation so the outside dose stays low.

q: After three or four years in a reactor, spent fuel must be removed and replaced with a new one because the amount of uranium-235 in it has fallen and the fission products has _____.
e: After three or four years in a reactor, spent fuel must be removed and replaced with a new one because the amount of uranium-235 in it has fallen and the fission products has built up. Put disappeared or stabilized in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Fission splits a heavy nucleus after a neutron bite, throwing fragments and more neutrons.

q: Many of the fission products are radioactive and dangerous, and strontium-90 becomes concentrated in the _____.
e: Many of the fission products are radioactive and dangerous, and strontium-90 becomes concentrated in the bones. thyroid is not bones, and lungs is not bones either. Fission splits a heavy nucleus after a neutron bite, throwing fragments and more neutrons.

q: Iodine-131 is a dangerous fission product that becomes concentrated in the _____ gland.
e: Iodine-131 is a dangerous fission product that becomes concentrated in the thyroid gland. Put pituitary or adrenal in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Fission splits a heavy nucleus after a neutron bite, throwing fragments and more neutrons.

q: Many of the fission products are radioactive and dangerous to be released into the environment, and these include strontium-90, iodine-131 and _____.
e: Many of the fission products are radioactive and dangerous to be released into the environment, and these include strontium-90, iodine-131 and plutonium-239. carbon-14 is not plutonium-239, and uranium-235 is not plutonium-239 either. Radioactivity is nuclear: an unstable nucleus emits alpha, beta, or gamma. Fission splits a heavy nucleus after a neutron bite, throwing fragments and more neutrons.

q: In an atomic bomb, an uncontrolled chain reaction takes place so that an extremely large amount of energy is released in a short interval of time, and when completely fissioned, 1 kg of uranium-235 releases energy equivalently produced by _____ tons of TNT.
e: In an atomic bomb, an uncontrolled chain reaction takes place so that an extremely large amount of energy is released in a short interval of time, and when completely fissioned, 1 kg of uranium-235 releases energy equivalently produced by 17 000 tons of TNT. Put 1 000 or 1 000 000 in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. A chain reaction is when fission neutrons go on to split further fuel nuclei.

q: The detonation of an atomic bomb releases enormous amounts of thermal energy, achieving temperatures of several million degrees Celsius, which creates a large fireball and a characteristic _____-shaped cloud.
e: The detonation of an atomic bomb releases enormous amounts of thermal energy, achieving temperatures of several million degrees Celsius, which creates a large fireball and a characteristic mushroom-shaped cloud. Put spherical or conical in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Celsius, which creates a large fireball and a characteristic _____-shaped cloud. mushroom.

q: The greenhouse gas emissions from nuclear fission power are much _____ than those associated with coal, oil and gas.
e: The greenhouse gas emissions from nuclear fission power are much smaller than those associated with coal, oil and gas. Put larger or equal in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. Fission splits a heavy nucleus after a neutron bite, throwing fragments and more neutrons.

q: A catastrophic risk potential in nuclear reactors can be brought about by overheated fuels melting and releasing large quantities of fission products into the environment, which is known as _____.
e: A catastrophic risk potential in nuclear reactors can be brought about by overheated fuels melting and releasing large quantities of fission products into the environment, which is known as meltdown. fusion is not meltdown, and criticality is not meltdown either. A reactor is a vessel where a fission chain can be started, held, and steered.

q: The 1979 Three Mile Island accident and 1986 _____ disaster ended the rapid growth of global nuclear power capacity.
e: The 1979 Three Mile Island accident and 1986 Chernobyl disaster ended the rapid growth of global nuclear power capacity. Put Fukushima or Hiroshima in the gap and the sentence describes the wrong physics. The year 1979 belongs to this fact, not a nearby discovery date.

q: A release of radioactive materials followed the 2011 Japanese tsunami which damaged the _____ Nuclear Power Plant.
e: A release of radioactive materials followed the 2011 Japanese tsunami which damaged the Fukushima I Nuclear Power Plant. Chernobyl is not Fukushima I, and Three Mile Island is not Fukushima I either. Radioactivity is nuclear: an unstable nucleus emits alpha, beta, or gamma.
